title: The perfection of wisdom
hookLine: the long wisdom sutras, from eight thousand lines to one letter "a"
last: SKILLFUL MEANS: THE TEACHING FITTED TO THE LISTENER.

cards: One Mahayana sutra is named for its length: the Perfection of Wisdom in a Hundred Thousand Lines. Another is the Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines.
And at the far end of the same family sits the Perfection of Wisdom in One Letter, in which the Buddha gives the whole teaching as a single sound: the letter a.
Somewhere in between is a page short enough to read before the kettle boils. Same subject, wildly different sizes.

teach.b: First, a family. The perfection of wisdom isn't one book.
It's a family of Mahayana sutras with one subject: the wisdom that sees all things as empty of a fixed, separate self, and the bodhisattva who walks the path with that wisdom and with compassion.
Which came first, the long ones or the short ones, is a question for historians.
Second, why so many sizes. One way to hear it borrows yesterday's word. Some people have the time and the hunger for a hundred thousand lines.
Some need a page. Some need one breath. The teaching shrinks or grows to fit whoever receives it, the way a doctor fits the dose.
Third, the page. The Heart Sutra is the short one this path read slowly in its first year.
One of its lines, in plain words: form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.
The things you see and touch are real enough to bump into, and also not solid, separate things standing alone. And that open, connected way things are isn't somewhere else.
It's right here, as the cup and the hand and the floor. Fourth, the letter. In the One Letter text, the Buddha says the perfection of wisdom is held in the letter a.

Some teachers point out that in Sanskrit, a short a at the front of a word can turn it into its opposite: himsa is harm, ahimsa is non-harm. So one small sound can say not to every fixed idea we carry.
From a hundred thousand lines to one letter, only the size of the doorway changes.

how: Mahayana communities in East Asia and Tibet chant the Heart Sutra, and some monasteries read or recite the longer perfection of wisdom sutras on special days.

games.q: what does “the perfection of wisdom” mean?
o: a perfect memory of every sutra the Buddha ever taught
a family of sutras on the wisdom that sees things as empty
the wisdom an old person gains from a long, full life

games.q: from long to short: tap the pairs.
p: a sutra named for its length
a page before the kettle boils
the whole teaching in one sound
a short a that turns harm into non-harm

s: the perfection of wisdom is a single book
it's a family of sutras, from a hundred thousand lines down to one letter.
one text gives the whole teaching as the letter a
the Perfection of Wisdom in One Letter.
the Heart Sutra treats form and emptiness as two separate things
form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.

games.q: you want the perfection of wisdom. you're offered the sutra in a hundred thousand lines, the page-long Heart Sutra, or the single letter a. which one holds the teaching?
o: only the longest; the short ones leave things out
only the shortest; the long ones are padding
all of them; the doorway changes size, not the wisdom
games.why: the family keeps them all, long and short, as one perfection of wisdom fitted to different readers.

practice: Take one line from the Heart Sutra, form is emptiness, emptiness is form, and say it once, slowly, in your head; no copy needed.

Then look at one thing in front of you, your hand, a cup, the floor, and set the line beside it without trying to work it out. Then let even the line go, and rest with the breath, short as a single letter.

wordCard.voice: The perfection of wisdom. A family of Mahayana sutras on the wisdom that sees things as they are, from a hundred thousand lines to a single letter. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the short a, the one letter in which, in one sutra, the whole perfection of wisdom is given.

carryVoice: Your line: from long to short. The whole teaching can fit in one letter. See you tomorrow.
